figures.caption: Table 1: The structural priors compared (pooled over λ; paired same-seed speedups; * = at λ=1.0). Whether generalization occurs tracks feature-family alignment; label-free invariance content suffices for accelerating; a brief early window or a norm clamp removes the supervised prior’s stall mode.

Figure 1: Survival curves for windowed application of the prior (λ=1.0). Applying SupCon only during epochs [0, 2k] (4% of budget) generalizes 10/10 at a median 2.7× speedup, outperforming continuous application (8/10, 1.25×), λ-annealing (1.7×), and — at matched 2,000-epoch duration — the late window [2k, 4k] (2.1×); the longer late window [2k, 10k] is reliable but slower still (1.9×). Norm-clamp reference in brown.

Figure 2: Epochs to generalization versus clamped total weight norm (log scale; 3 seeds per value). Plain cross-entropy (black) follows a steep delay-law exponential — slope 0.344 per unit norm, 31× per +10, a lower bound since its highest-norm cells are entirely censored — while the structural prior (red) is nearly flat (slope 0.020, 1.22× per +10). Structure injection flattens the weight-norm delay law by ∼17× in the exponent. Both curves share a low-norm floor below ∼40–45.
